title: The Decoy Effect

scenes.text: Why do you always buy the *medium* popcorn?
scenes.vo: Why do you almost always end up buying the medium popcorn?
Say a cinema sells small popcorn for 150 rupees and large for 300. Most people pick small. Large feels like too much.
Now the cinema adds a medium for 270.
Suddenly your brain thinks: wait, large is only 30 rupees more than medium? That's a great deal! And you buy the large.
The medium was never meant to be bought. It's a trap, there only to make the large look cheap.
Scientists call this the decoy effect. A decoy is a fake option that pushes you towards the one the seller wants.

scenes.text: You'll see it on menus, phone plans and app subscriptions
scenes.vo: Look closely and you'll find it everywhere. Menus, phone plans, app subscriptions.

scenes.text: Ask: would I still pick this if the middle option *wasn't there*?
scenes.vo: So next time, ask yourself: would I still pick this if the middle option wasn't there?

caption:
That medium popcorn isn't there for you to buy. 🍿 It's there to make the large look cheap! It's called the decoy effect, and once you see it, you'll spot it everywhere.

Tag a friend who always buys the large 👇
source: Huber, Payne & Puto (1982), Journal of Consumer Research; Ariely, D. (2008), Predictably Irrational, ch. 1.
